what_its_for: Asfotase alfa is used to treat a rare inherited disease called hypophosphatasia (HPP). HPP is a condition where your body cannot properly build and maintain strong bones and teeth because of low levels of a special enzyme. This medicine replaces that missing enzyme and helps your bones and teeth develop and stay strong. It is used in babies, children, teenagers, and adults who have the perinatal (before birth), infantile (in infancy), or juvenile (childhood) form of this disease.
how_to_take: Asfotase alfa is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection). A healthcare provider will teach you or a caregiver how to give this injection at home. Common injection sites include the stomach area (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate (change) the injection site each time to avoid skin irritation. Do not inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, hard, or scarred. Gently mix the medicine by slowly turning the vial upside down — do NOT shake it vigorously, as this can damage the medicine. Always check the liquid before injecting; it should be clear to slightly cloudy and colorless to pale yellow with no large particles.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your body weight. The usual doses are either 2 mg per kilogram (kg) of body weight given 3 times per week, OR 1 mg per kg of body weight given 6 times per week. Your doctor may adjust your dose as needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember on the same day. Then go back to your regular schedule. Do not give two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store asfotase alfa in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze it. Keep the vials in their original carton to protect them from light. Once removed from the refrigerator, the medicine can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 3 hours. Do not use the medicine if it has been left at room temperature for more than 3 hours. Throw away (dispose of) any unused medicine in the vial after each injection — do not save leftover medicine for later use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not shake the vial vigorously, as this can damage the medicine. Avoid injecting into the same spot every time — always rotate your injection sites. Do not use the medicine if it looks abnormal (large particles, unusual color) or if the expiration date has passed. Do not freeze the medicine or expose it to extreme heat. Avoid skipping doses without talking to your doctor first, as consistent treatment is important for the best results.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a serious allergic reaction (signs include hives, rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness, fast heartbeat, or feeling faint); severe skin reactions or sores at the injection site that do not heal; signs of abnormal calcium levels such as muscle cramps, numbness or tingling, seizures, or irregular heartbeat; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also contact your doctor if you have any questions about how to prepare or give the injection.
when_it_works: Asfotase alfa does not work overnight. It takes time for your body to respond. Some improvements in breathing, bone strength, and physical ability may be noticed within weeks to months. However, full benefits — such as better bone development and improved ability to walk and move — may take many months or even years of regular treatment. It is very important to keep using this medicine as directed even if you do not feel different right away. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and tests.
special_populations: Children and Infants: This medicine is approved for use in babies and children and has been specifically studied in pediatric patients with HPP. Doses are based on body weight, so children's doses will be lower than adult doses. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if asfotase alfa can harm an unborn baby or pass into breast milk. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medicine. Kidney or Liver Problems: There is limited information about using this medicine in patients with significant kidney or liver problems. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions so they can decide if this medicine is safe for you.
